modelName: Online Return and Refund Product Model
modelPurpose: Represents a long-running return and refund duty across eligibility, parcel movement, warehouse inspection, refund issuance, and truthful customer status.

product.name: Online Store
product.description: A product that lets customers return eligible delivered items and receive refunds according to policy.

lexicon.definition: A world-anchored obligation or capability the product must support, expressed as the KR title.
examples: Reserve an available book copy for pickup
Prepare a paid cafe order for customer pickup
Return an eligible delivered item and issue the correct refund

lexicon.definition: The canonical end-to-end path that fulfills one primary duty, expressed as the KR description.
examples: A member searches for a book, reserves a copy, and receives pickup details.

lexicon.definition: An atomic behavioral transition with preconditions, trigger, and observable postconditions.
examples: Given a copy is available, when a member reserves it, then one active hold is created.

lexicon.definition: A measurable indicator of user-experienced quality, such as latency, correctness, freshness, or recoverability.
A threshold target for a UX SLI that defines acceptable experience for a critical duty or journey.
examples: 99% of valid reservations confirm in under one second.

lexicon.definition: A concrete end-to-end execution example that demonstrates correct behavior for a duty journey.
examples: Successful reservation of one available library copy.

lexicon.definition: A concrete execution example that demonstrates forbidden, failed, misleading, or unacceptable behavior.
examples: Two members receive confirmation for the same physical copy.

lexicon.definition: A domain entity that exists or is meaningful in the real world and anchors the product architecture.
An architectural separation justified by real-world duration, externality, or human/physical delay.
examples: Kitchen preparation may be asynchronous because cooking takes real-world time.

lexicon.definition: A product law that must remain true across all valid states and transitions.
examples: One accepted return may issue at most one refund.

ambiguityPolicy.principle: The model must be internally decidable. If ambiguity remains, the model must name the missing external fact instead of hiding uncertainty in vague wording.
requiresClarificationWhen: A duty cannot be mapped to at least one real-world object or interaction.
A network boundary lacks a real-world latency or causality justification.
A trace can be interpreted as both golden and anti-golden.
A weakening or breaking update lacks explicit compatibility classification.
A journey completion criterion cannot be evaluated from observable state.

objects.name: Customer
objects.definition: A person who bought a delivered item and may request a return.

objects.name: Delivered Item
objects.definition: A specific item from an order that has reached the customer.

objects.name: Return Request
objects.definition: A request to return a delivered item under policy.

objects.name: Parcel
objects.definition: The physical package containing the returned item.

objects.name: Inspection Result
objects.definition: A decision about whether the returned item meets acceptance policy.

objects.name: Refund
objects.definition: A money movement back to the customer according to return policy.

interactions.name: Create return request
interactions.description: The customer creates a return request for an eligible delivered item.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Eligibility and request creation should be fast digital operations.

interactions.name: Ship return parcel
interactions.description: The customer gives the parcel to a carrier and it moves to the warehouse.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Parcel movement occurs over hours or days.

interactions.name: Inspect returned item
interactions.description: Warehouse determines whether the returned item is accepted.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Inspection takes operational time and may involve humans.

interactions.name: Issue refund
interactions.description: The product initiates refund after accepted return.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Payment networks can take hours or days.

invariants.name: Refund only after accepted return
invariants.statement: A refund must not be issued before the return is accepted unless instant refund policy is explicitly modeled.
invariants.rationale: The business should not refund items that were never accepted.

invariants.name: Refund idempotency
invariants.statement: One accepted return may issue at most one refund for the same refundable obligation.
invariants.rationale: Retries must not cause duplicate money movement.

networkBoundaries.name: Return creation boundary
networkBoundaries.description: Eligibility and return creation must be causally tight.
networkBoundaries.realWorldProcess: A customer asks the business to accept a returned delivered item.
networkBoundaries.causalityJustification: Creating a return request creates a business obligation and must be linked to eligibility.
networkBoundaries.userVisibleImpact: The customer immediately sees whether the return can start.
networkBoundaries.failureMode: An ineligible item may receive a return request.

networkBoundaries.name: Carrier shipping boundary
networkBoundaries.description: Parcel movement progresses asynchronously through carrier events.
networkBoundaries.realWorldProcess: A physical parcel moves through a carrier network.
networkBoundaries.causalityJustification: Shipping is physically slow and externally observed through scans.
networkBoundaries.userVisibleImpact: The customer sees in-transit updates after carrier imports.
networkBoundaries.failureMode: Delayed scans can make status temporarily stale.

networkBoundaries.name: Inspection and refund boundary
networkBoundaries.description: Inspection and refund processing happen asynchronously after warehouse receipt.
networkBoundaries.realWorldProcess: Warehouse accepts the item and payment rails process refund.
networkBoundaries.causalityJustification: Inspection and payment settlement involve real-world and external delays.
networkBoundaries.userVisibleImpact: The customer sees accepted, refund issued, and posting states.
networkBoundaries.failureMode: A retry bug can cause duplicate refund if idempotency is broken.

objectives.title: Make returns trustworthy and correctly refundable
objectives.description: Customers understand return eligibility, return progress, inspection result, and refund status.
objectives.successMeaning: Eligible items can be returned, accepted returns are refunded once, and customers see truthful status.

duties.title: Return an eligible delivered item and issue the correct refund
duties.intent: Allow a customer to return an eligible delivered item and receive exactly the refund owed.
duties.scope: Covers return creation, shipping progress, inspection, refund issuance, and customer-visible status.

okrMapping.keyResultTitle: Return an eligible delivered item and issue the correct refund
okrMapping.keyResultDescription: A customer creates a return, ships the item, the item is accepted, and the correct refund is issued once.

journeys.title: Return item and receive refund
journeys.description: A customer requests a return for an eligible delivered item, ships it back, the warehouse accepts it, and one correct refund is issued.
journeys.purpose: Preserve trust across a long-running process involving goods, warehouse operations, and money movement.
journeys.trigger: Customer selects a delivered item to return.
preconditions: The item is eligible under policy.
primaryFlow: Refund is approved and issued once.
completionCriteria: Return reaches accepted or rejected state.
If accepted, exactly one refund is issued.
Customer-visible status reflects current authoritative state.
variants: Manual review may occur before acceptance.
failureBoundaries: Rejected inspection does not issue refund unless policy override exists.
Refund provider retry must not duplicate refund.
nonGoals: Exchange and warranty workflows are separate duties.

timing.causalJustification: Return creation needs immediate consistency, while shipping, inspection, and refund settlement take real-world time.

flow.notes: Linear primary flow derived from step order.

steps.title: Create return request
steps.given: A delivered item is eligible for return.
steps.when: The customer confirms the return reason.
steps.then: The system creates a return request and shows shipping instructions.
thenAssertions: The return request references one delivered item.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees that the return has started.

stateTransitions.notes: Item is marked return-requested once a return request is created.
A return request record is created.

steps.title: Update parcel in transit
steps.given: A carrier scan exists for the parcel.
steps.then: The return status updates to in transit.
thenAssertions: The scan references the correct return request.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees that the parcel is moving back.

stateTransitions.notes: Item is in transit back to warehouse.

steps.title: Inspect returned item
steps.given: The warehouse receives the return parcel.
steps.then: The system records passed, failed, or manual review.
thenAssertions: Inspection result exists before refund approval when required.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees review or acceptance status.

stateTransitions.notes: Inspection begins; result is pending until decision.

steps.title: Approve refund after accepted inspection
steps.then: The system approves the refund for the correct amount.
thenAssertions: Refund approval references the accepted return.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees refund approved or processing.

stateTransitions.notes: Refund becomes approved after successful inspection.

steps.title: Issue refund once
steps.given: A refund is approved and no refund has already been issued for the same return.
steps.then: The system issues exactly one refund.
thenAssertions: Duplicate retries do not issue duplicate refunds.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees refund issued and expected posting information.

stateTransitions.notes: Return request closes after refund issuance.
Item becomes refunded after refund issuance.

steps.title: Reject failed inspection
steps.then: The system rejects the return and does not issue refund.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees rejection reason and no refund promise.

stateTransitions.notes: Refund remains not approved when inspection fails.
Return request is rejected when inspection fails.

slis.name: Return request creation time
slis.description: Time from confirming return to seeing return instructions.

slis.name: Refund trigger latency
slis.description: Time from accepted inspection to refund issuance request.

slis.name: Customer status correctness
slis.description: Percentage of status views that match authoritative return and refund state.

slos.name: Return request under two seconds
slos.consequenceOfViolation: Customers may retry and create duplicate confusion.

slos.name: Refund triggered within one hour
slos.consequenceOfViolation: Accepted returns are not promptly refunded.

slos.name: Customer status correctness
slos.consequenceOfViolation: Customers may be misled about money or returned goods.

golden.title: Successful return and refund
golden.description: A customer returns an eligible item, warehouse accepts it, and one refund is issued.
golden.scenario: The item is eligible and passes inspection.
golden.finalState: Return is accepted and one refund is issued.
golden.classificationReason: The trace satisfies acceptance-before-refund and refund idempotency.

antiGolden.title: Refund before required inspection
antiGolden.description: A refund is issued before the parcel is received or inspected.
antiGolden.scenario: Policy requires inspection but refund is issued after return creation.

antiGolden.title: Duplicate refund from retry
antiGolden.description: A retry job issues the same refund twice.
antiGolden.scenario: Refund provider retry occurs after first refund issued.
antiGolden.finalState: Two refunds exist for one accepted return.

updates.summary: Initial model for returning an eligible item and issuing the correct refund.
updates.reason: Establishes the first complete version of this product representation.
updates.rolloutPlan: Adopt as baseline after schema and semantic validation.
